label: rem:categorical-neutrality-saturated-shells-interpretation
title: Self-conjugate support, the dropped locality assumption, and operator-level vs character-sum reading
html:
Structural constraint

The full-twist \Delta_n^2 acts on each Wedderburn block V_\lambda of H_n(q) by the central scalar q^{c(\lambda)}, where c(\lambda) = \sum_{x \in \lambda}(j_x - i_x) provides the content sum of the partition \lambda \vdash n [geckpfeiffer2000, mathas1999]. Trivial action of the full-twist on \Phi_n restricts the partitions in the Wedderburn decomposition of \Phi_n to those with content sum zero. These form the self-conjugate partitions \lambda = \lambda' on Young's lattice. At saturated n, \Phi_n finds support strictly on self-conjugate partitions.

For n \notin \mathfrak{M}, the constraint fails. Non-self-conjugate partitions enter \Phi_n, and the full-twist acts by a non-trivial scalar. This transition formalizes shell closure, replacing ad hoc selection rules with categorical constraints.

Homological reformulation

The Hoefsmit seminormal form (prop:hoefsmit-seminormal-form) supplies explicit matrices for \sigma_i on each V_\lambda. Direct multiplication recovers the full-twist eigenvalue q^{c(\lambda)}. Numerical verification at k = 3, \dots, 10 confirms the shell pattern at small magic values n = 2, 8, 20. At k \geq 12, combinatorial growth in |\{\lambda \vdash n\}| blocks matrix evaluation.

The conjecture reformulates this homologically. Instead of verifying \Phi_n with matrices, we verify the self-conjugate-support condition via content-sum arithmetic. This approach accesses saturation at n \in \{50, 82, 126\} without matrix multiplication.

Global topological neutrality

Earlier models (atom-knot-mass-derivation) treated \Phi_n as a local object. They required "screening" or "local trivialisation" to explain shell closure. This refactor abandons the locality assumption. We identify \Phi_n as the global section of the mass functor over \mathbf{C} (rem:phi-n-global-section). A non-trivial full-twist action propagates unbounded ribbon flux through the brane tower. Finite observable mass demands global topological neutrality at saturation.

Operator-level support

The claim that \Phi_n receives support on self-conjugate partitions applies at the operator level. The categorical mass operator \Phi_n exhibits zero matrix entries on every non-self-conjugate isotypical component in H_n(q) = \bigoplus_\lambda \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda).

This does not imply the Plancherel-weighted character sum:

\sum_{\lambda = \lambda'} w_\lambda \cdot \chi^\lambda(\beta_{\mathrm{atom}}).

The character sum vanishes identically at certain atomic-braid cycle types. The binding-energy enhancement at magic shells derives from the non-vanishing of \Phi_n on the self-conjugate isotypical operator blocks. Empirically, the GS-filtration Term 6 plus an is_magic_pair operator-correction captures the magic-shell signal, correlating at +0.74 to the AME residual.

Discussion

Numerical witnesses at k = 3, \dots, 10 support the saturation condition. The conjecture extends this to all n \in \mathfrak{M}, including the high-mass region \{50, 82, 126\}.

The downstream cone includes conj:magic-numbers-from-q and the shell-closure portion of the BW formula (thm:wedderburn-mass-formula). Proving these requires either a derivation of this conjecture or its retention as a class-axiomatised input.
